clue.text: Sole declaration of principle

definitions.meaning: the thick raised sole of a chunky shoe
a party's published set of policies

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are standard: a thick shoe sole, and a political party's statement of policies.

clue.text: Soft touch on breast, I admitted, was most irregular

parts.note: a pat is a light, gentle touch

indicators.note: the word for breast lets in the letter I

parts.note: the chest is the breast

explanation.surface: A gentle touch on someone's chest was highly improper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'admitted' puts I inside CHEST. The definition reads 'was most irregular' as the superlative adjective 'most patchy'.
explanation.definitionFit: Patchiest is the superlative of patchy, meaning most uneven or irregular in quality.

clue.text: Was most anxious to treat despair

indicators.note: to treat is to process, here reworking the letters of the word

explanation.surface: Someone was very keen to cure another person's despair.
explanation.definitionFit: To aspire is to long eagerly for something, so the past tense means was very eager.

clue.text: Look for food scrap, as enemy's prisoner

indicators.note: the scrap is held captive within the enemy

parts.note: a foe is an enemy; the 's means has
a rag is a scrap of cloth

explanation.surface: Searching for something to eat, a scrap is held by a hostile captor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'enemy's prisoner' reads as the enemy has the scrap held captive, the 's standing for has; 'as' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To forage is to search widely for food or provisions.

clue.text: Dealing with carcass is a performance

definitions.meaning: melting down animal remains for fat
an interpretation of a piece of music or drama

explanation.definitionFit: Rendering is processing carcasses for fat, and also a performance or interpretation of a work.

clue.text: Clever chap, to hide in so great a tree

indicators.note: the clever chap is concealed inside the words for so great

parts.note: such as in 'such a fuss' means so great
MA, a Master of Arts, is a learned man

explanation.surface: A bright fellow tries to conceal himself inside an enormous tree.
explanation.walkthrough: MA (Master of Arts) is crossword shorthand for a learned person. This spelling is an older form of sumac, a shrub or small tree.
explanation.definitionFit: Sumach is a shrub or small tree grown for its foliage and spice berries.

clue.text: Cat sees I am troubled

indicators.note: troubled means disturbed, so the letters are stirred up

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A cat perceives that the speaker is upset.
explanation.definitionFit: The Siamese is a well-known breed of cat from Thailand.

clue.text: Unrivalled, unlike Andersen's poor little girl?

definitions.meaning: Hans Christian Andersen's Little Match Girl had matches; her opposite would have none

explanation.definitionFit: Matchless means without equal, and literally means having no matches, unlike the Little Match Girl.

clue.text: Sugar mountain covers area

indicators.note: the mountain sits over and around the letter for area

parts.note: Mount Carmel is a mountain range in Israel

explanation.surface: A mountain blanketed with sugar over a district.
explanation.definitionFit: Caramel is sugar heated until it melts and browns.

clue.text: Dump tiny reward

definitions.meaning: a rubbish heap or refuse site
a small gratuity given for service

explanation.definitionFit: A rubbish dump is a tip in Britain, and a tip is also a small gratuity.

clue.text: Amazing: me starring in circus role

indicators.note: something amazing astonishes, read as the letters being thrown into confusion

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A performer boasts that their own starring turn in the circus is amazing.
explanation.definitionFit: The ringmaster is the circus official who introduces the acts in the ring.

clue.text: I'm starting, say, to get into Ivanhoe and the like

indicators.note: the abbreviation for say enters the word for Ivanhoe's kind

parts.note: Ivanhoe is the hero of Scott's novel, so such figures are heroes
EG, for example, abbreviates exempli gratia

explanation.surface: Someone announces they are beginning to read Scott's Ivanhoe and similar novels.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the exclamation said when starting something daunting; 'I'm starting, say' pretends to be the opening of a sentence.
explanation.definitionFit: The exclamation is what someone says just before beginning something risky, an idiom equivalent.

clue.text: Raise the dead

parts.note: not resurrection but digging up a buried body

explanation.definitionFit: To dig a corpse out of its grave is literally to bring the dead up from the ground.

clue.text: Ibsen heroine losing husband, in the Norse story

indicators.note: the heroine's name drops a letter for her spouse

parts.note: Hedda Gabler is the title heroine of Ibsen's play

explanation.surface: A Scandinavian heroine loses her husband in an old Norse tale.
explanation.definitionFit: The Edda is a medieval Icelandic collection of Old Norse poems and myths.

clue.text: One of dry humour?

parts.note: dry here means teetotal, and humour an old word for disposition

explanation.definitionFit: A teetotaller avoids alcohol, so is dry, and humour once meant temperament.

clue.text: Charming bride from ugly family?

parts.note: Prince Charming's bride in the fairy tale, whose stepsisters are ugly

explanation.definitionFit: In the pantomime story the heroine marries Prince Charming despite her Ugly Sisters.

clue.text: Short vestment on an animal spotted

indicators.note: the vestment's word is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: a dalmatic is a wide-sleeved liturgical tunic worn by deacons
taken as written

explanation.surface: A brief church garment is seen on an animal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short' removes the last letter, C, of DALMATIC.
explanation.definitionFit: The Dalmatian is a dog breed famous for its black or liver spots on white.

clue.text: A jolly powerful trumpeter

parts.note: a Jolly is slang for a Royal Marine, RM
strong means powerful

explanation.surface: A very strong trumpet player.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jolly' is old naval slang for a Royal Marine. Louis Armstrong was the jazz trumpeter.
explanation.definitionFit: Louis Armstrong was the celebrated New Orleans jazz trumpet player.

clue.text: Play shows what Xenophon's troops sought: a dupe

parts.note: Xenophon's Greek army famously cried 'Thalatta!' on reaching the sea
to gull is to dupe or deceive; a gull is a dupe

explanation.surface: A drama portrays the goal of Xenophon's marching Greek soldiers as a fool's errand.
explanation.walkthrough: In the Anabasis, the retreating Ten Thousand sought the sea and shouted for joy on sighting it. Chekhov wrote the play.
explanation.definitionFit: Chekhov's well-known four-act drama has this title, so it is an example of a play.

clue.text: I wrongly believe this place comes with endless credit

parts.note: here means this place

indicators.note: the word for credit loses its final letter

parts.note: on tick means on credit

explanation.surface: Someone confesses to false beliefs about a place that offers easy credit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' takes K from TICK, British slang for credit. The definition is what a heretic might say of themself.
explanation.definitionFit: A heretic holds beliefs contrary to orthodox doctrine, so in the eyes of the church believes wrongly.

clue.text: One receives bill at my school

indicators.note: the word for one takes in the word for bill

parts.note: an ace is a one in cards or dice
an ad is an advertising bill or poster
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone accepts a bill at their own school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'receives' signals the container; 'at' is a link word joining the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: An academy is a school, especially one for special training.

clue.text: Fraud in singular university stream

parts.note: S abbreviates singular in grammar
the Cam is the river flowing through Cambridge

explanation.surface: A swindle takes place in a lone river by a university town.
explanation.definitionFit: A scam is a swindle or confidence trick, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Composer filmed on the mandolin

definitions.meaning: Arcangelo, the Italian Baroque violinist and composer
Captain ____'s Mandolin, the 2001 film of de Bernieres's novel

explanation.definitionFit: Corelli was a Baroque composer, and the name is in the title of the film Captain Corelli's Mandolin.

clue.text: To be delayed speaking gives a sense of oppression

indicators.note: spoken out, the word for being delayed sounds like a different word

parts.note: to wait is to be held up

explanation.surface: Being held up while talking feels burdensome.
explanation.walkthrough: 'speaking' signals a soundalike: WAIT said out loud.
explanation.definitionFit: A weight on one's mind is a burden, a feeling of being oppressed.

clue.text: Near Madagascar, limited the force of the sea

indicators.note: the letters are confined within the run of the two words

explanation.surface: Close to Madagascar, a naval force was restricted.
explanation.definitionFit: An armada is a fleet of warships, a naval force.

clue.text: To demonstrate humanity, a scientist's brought round little furry creature

indicators.note: the scientist's name is placed around the other pieces

parts.note: James Watt, the Scottish engineer and scientist
'to err is human', so erring shows one's humanity

explanation.surface: To prove they are human, a researcher is revived after fainting near a small furry animal.
explanation.walkthrough: The proverb 'to err is human' supplies the humanity. The creature, actually a water vole, is Ratty in The Wind in the Willows.
explanation.definitionFit: The water rat is a small furry riverbank rodent, so fits the description of a creature.

clue.text: Nun involved in significant work once linking us with France

definitions.text: work once linking us with France

indicators.note: the shuffled letters sit within the word for significant

parts.note: a telling detail is a significant one

indicators.note: involved means tangled, so the letters are muddled

explanation.surface: A nun takes part in important engineering that once joined Britain to France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involved' rearranges the nun, and 'in' puts the result inside the word for significant. The definition refers to the Channel Tunnel digging.
explanation.definitionFit: Excavating the Channel Tunnel, which connects England with France, was boring under the sea.

clue.text: Stars in Tolstoy

definitions.meaning: a constellation of the zodiac, the Lion

explanation.definitionFit: The Lion constellation has this name, and it is also the Russian novelist's given name.

clue.text: Sailor at first with the bends, an old naval problem

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the sailor is taken

parts.note: full of bends means curvy

explanation.surface: A sailor at the beginning suffers decompression sickness, an old maritime affliction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The bends' suggests divers' decompression sickness; here it just means curves.
explanation.definitionFit: Scurvy, from lack of vitamin C, was the classic disease of sailors on long voyages.

clue.text: Providing stuff to clothe any number joining up

indicators.note: the word for providing kit wraps around the letter for a number

parts.note: kitting out means supplying equipment or gear
N is the mathematical symbol for an indefinite number

explanation.surface: Supplying material to dress a crowd of people as they enlist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to clothe' places N inside KITTING, after the K.
explanation.definitionFit: Broken bones knitting are joining together, and knitting also joins loops of yarn.
